extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, assignees, and USPTO examiners/assignment-division staff involved in recording and correcting assignment/ownership records
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing recordation of assignment/other title-affecting documents at the USPTO, correction/expungement of recorded items, and establishment of an assignee's right to take action in patent/trademark matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents for recordation
rubrics_metrics.description: A party wishing recordation of a document with respect to additional patents/applications must submit: (A) a copy of the original document (may be previously recorded papers showing reel and frame numbers, or a copy thereof); (B) a completed cover sheet (see 37 CFR 3.31 and MPEP § 302.07); and (C) the appropriate recording fee (see 37 CFR 1.21(h) and 3.41).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will assign a new recording date, update the assignment database, and microfilm the cover sheet and document to become part of the official record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and formal compliance for recording (recording date)
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of recording is the date the document meeting the requirements for recording set forth in the regulations is filed in the Office. A document that does not comply with the identification requirements of 37 CFR 3.21 will not be recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents missing other requirements (e.g., completed cover sheet or required fee) will be returned for correction when a correspondence address is available. Returned papers are stamped with the original receipt date and, if corrected and resubmitted within the specified period, the Office will consider the original date of filing as the date of recording (see 37 CFR 3.51 and use of 37 CFR 1.8/1.10 for postal proof). The specified period to resubmit will not be extended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of recording does not determine validity or title
rubrics_metrics.description: The recording of a document pursuant to § 3.11 is not a determination by the Office of the validity of the document or the effect that document has on the title to an application, a patent, or a registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When necessary, the Office will determine what effect a document has, including whether a party has authority to take action in a matter pending before the Office (see MPEP § 324).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of conditional assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments conditional on performance of acts/events (e.g., payment) if recorded are regarded by the Office as absolute assignments for Office purposes until canceled by written consent of all parties or by court decree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office does not determine whether the condition has been fulfilled; submission for recordation is treated as signifying the act/event has occurred. A security agreement that does not convey right, title and interest is not a conditional assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment documents should not be placed in application/patent files
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment documents submitted for recording should not be placed directly in application or patent files, but should be forwarded to the Assignment Division for recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title report usage and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'title report' can be used by the Assignment Division under certain circumstances to report the owner of an application or patent as shown by Assignment Division records at the date the title report is made. Title reports are not orderable by applicants/attorneys; examiners may obtain one internally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The public can request a certified abstract of title for a fee (37 CFR 1.19(b)(4)). See MPEP § 301.01 for which assignment records are publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective document requirements for correcting errors in recorded assignment documents
rubrics_metrics.description: An error in a recorded assignment document will be corrected by Assignment Division provided a 'corrective document' is submitted that includes: (A) a copy of the original assignment document with the corrections made therein, the corrections initialed and dated by the conveying party; and (B) a new Recordation Form Cover Sheet (form PTO-1595).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The new cover sheet must identify the submission as a 'corrective document' and indicate the reel and frame number where the incorrect document appears. The person signing must state the information is true and that any copy is a true copy of the original. The corrective document will be recorded and given a new reel/frame number and recording date; recording fee required for each patent/application (37 CFR 1.21(h)). Corrections may be made on the original document (e.g., lining out incorrect numbers). If assignor unavailable, assignee may submit an affidavit/declaration with copy of recorded papers, a cover sheet, and required fee (see In re Abacab).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of cover sheet errors (37 CFR 3.34)
rubrics_metrics.description: An error in a cover sheet will be corrected only if (a) the error is apparent when the cover sheet is compared with the recorded document to which it pertains and (b) a corrected cover sheet is filed for recordation accompanied by a copy of the originally submitted document and the recording fee (37 CFR 3.34).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During recording the Assignment Services Division checks that a cover sheet is complete and records data exactly as it appears; it does not compare the cover sheet to the assignment document. Typographical errors made by the Office will be corrected promptly and without charge upon written request. For other errors the recording party must refile and pay the fees using procedures in MPEP § 323.01(a)-(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographical error distinction and effect on recordation date
rubrics_metrics.description: Typographical errors in a recorded cover sheet that do not affect title will be corrected and the recording party may keep the original date of recordation. If the typographical error affects title, the recording party will not keep the original date; the Assignment Services Division will correct automated records and change the date of recordation to the date the corrected cover sheet was received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To correct a typographical error in a recorded cover sheet submit: (A) a copy of the originally recorded assignment document (or other document affecting title); (B) a corrected cover sheet; and (C) the required fee for each application or patent (37 CFR 3.41). Submit original cover sheet to facilitate comparison; mark 'Other' and indicate correction nature and reel/frame if known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographical errors in recorded assignment documents (not cover sheet)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is an error in the recorded assignment document itself, the party responsible must either create and record a new document or make corrections to the original document and re-record it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an assignor is unavailable to correct or execute a new document, the assignee may submit an affidavit/declaration identifying the error and requesting correction, accompanied by a copy of the originally recorded papers, a cover sheet, and the required fee for each application or patent (37 CFR 3.41).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when assignment/name change improperly recorded by another party
rubrics_metrics.description: When an owner discovers another party has improperly recorded an assignment or name change (e.g., due to typographical error), the owner must correct the error by filing a corrected cover sheet with Assignment Services Division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner should (A) submit completed cover sheet identifying application/patent; (B) submit an affidavit/declaration identifying itself as correct owner, stating previously recorded document had erroneous information, and providing reel/frame of previous document; and (C) pay required fee (37 CFR 3.41) for each application/patent. Affidavit should include a summary of the true chain of title and a statement that original applicant/patentee or last correct assignee has been and continues to be owner. On corrected cover sheet check 'Other' and indicate correction and write correct owner in both conveying and receiving party boxes to show ownership never changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for expungement of assignment records
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions to correct, modify or 'expunge' assignment records are rarely granted and will be granted only if (A) normal corrective procedures will not provide adequate relief and (B) the integrity of the assignment records will not be affected by granting the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if expungement is granted for a particular application/patent, the image of the recorded document will remain in Assignment Services Division records at the same reel/frame; Office will delete links to the application/patent so the recorded document will not appear in searches for that application/patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may conduct prosecution / take action (37 CFR 3.71)
rubrics_metrics.description: One or more assignees may, after becoming of record pursuant to 3.73(c), conduct prosecution of a national patent application or reexamination proceeding to the exclusion of the inventive entity or prior assignees. The assignees who may conduct prosecution are: (1) a single assignee of the entire right, title and interest; or (2) two or more assignees who together own the entire right, title and interest. A partial assignee has less than the entire right, title and interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where partial assignees and/or inventors retain interests, all parties having any portion must join in taking action (act together as a composite entity) unless other provisions (e.g., petition under 37 CFR 1.47) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing ownership to take action (37 CFR 3.73(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: To request or take action in a patent or trademark matter, an assignee must establish ownership to the satisfaction of the Director by submitting a signed statement identifying the assignee accompanied by either (i) documentary evidence of a chain of title from the original owner to the assignee (e.g., copy of an executed assignment) or (ii) a statement specifying where such documentary evidence is recorded in the Office (e.g., reel and frame number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For patent matters documentary evidence must be accompanied by a statement affirming that the evidence was or concurrently is being submitted for recordation pursuant to 3.11; for trademark matters the documents may be required to be recorded as a condition to permitting the assignee to take action. The establishment may be combined with the paper requesting the action. The submission must be signed by a party authorized to act on behalf of the assignee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and sufficiency of 3.73(b) submissions for patents
rubrics_metrics.description: For patent matters, establishment of ownership must be submitted prior to, or at the same time as, the paper requesting or taking action; if absent the action will not be given effect. If the ownership submission is later filed, that later date will be the date of the request or action. An assignee of less than entire interest must indicate ownership extent (by percentage) or the Office may refuse to accept the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once 3.73(b) is complied with, the assignee may continue to take action without filing 3.73(b) each time, provided ownership has not changed. The 3.73(b) statement need not be duplicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who can sign the 3.73(b) submission (authorized signatory rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 3.73(b) submission must be signed by a party authorized to act on behalf of the assignee. For organizations, acceptable signatories include: (A) a person having apparent authority (officers such as CEO, president, vice-president, secretary, treasurer are presumed to have authority); (B) any person if the submission states the signer is authorized to act on behalf of the assignee; or (C) a person empowered by an organizational resolution if a copy of the resolution is or was submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles that do not clearly identify the signer as an officer (e.g., 'administrator', 'general counsel') are not presumed to have authority. A power of attorney to a patent practitioner does not make that practitioner an officer of the assignee or empower them to sign the submission on behalf of the assignee. If submission does not comply with (A)-(C), evidence of authority will be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing applications — ownership statement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When an assignee files a continuation or divisional application (other than a CPA under 1.53(d)), the application papers must either (A) refer to a statement filed under 3.73(b) in the parent application, (B) contain a copy of a 3.73(b) statement filed in the parent, or (C) contain a newly executed 3.73(b) statement. For a continuation-in-part by an assignee, a newly executed 3.73(b) must be filed. For a CPA, the parent 3.73(b) statement serves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of situations where ownership must or need not be established
rubrics_metrics.description: Situations requiring establishment under 3.73(b) include signing a reply to an Office action, signing a request for a CPA under 1.53(d) (unless prior statement exists and ownership unchanged), signing a terminal disclaimer, appointing own registered practitioner, giving a power to inspect, consenting to reissue or correction of inventorship, filing certain 1.47(b) applications, signing Fee(s) Transmittal, or requesting status of an application. Examples where ownership need not be established include signing a CPA when prior statement present and ownership unchanged, signing a small entity statement, signing a statement of common ownership, signing NASA/DOE property rights statement, filing certain affidavits where inventor unavailable, certificates under 1.8, or filing a request for reexamination under 1.510.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to MPEP sections cited for specific exceptions and interplay with previously filed 3.73(b) statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial assignees and joint action requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If no single assignee owns the entire right/title/interest, the application is owned by the combination of all partial assignees and any inventors who retained rights; the combination of all such parties is needed to conduct prosecution unless a petition under 1.47 has been granted or other rule provides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate that when a single assignee later becomes owner of entire interest (by assignment to one entity), that entity alone may conduct prosecution once made of record by a 3.73(b) statement indicating full ownership.
